rationales.quote: $50 a week?
rationales.explanation: Clarifies the subscription's pricing cadence.

rationales.quote: Why is that holding you back?
rationales.explanation: Probes the operational bottleneck limiting customer capacity.

rationales.quote: It seems like that becomes a real stumbling point.
rationales.explanation: Identifies styling and inventory operations as a potential execution obstacle.

rationales.quote: how many times you can turn that
rationales.explanation: Tests whether varied sizes and garments can be reused efficiently.

rationales.quote: what’s your acquisition cost?
rationales.explanation: Requests a key customer-acquisition efficiency metric.

rationales.quote: this is a customer acquisition business
rationales.explanation: Assesses marketing and customer acquisition as central to the business's success.

rationales.quote: Ideally it should be someone on your team.
rationales.explanation: Argues that marketing capability should be owned internally rather than outsourced.

rationales.quote: At a senior level.
rationales.explanation: Specifies that the required marketing hire must be senior.

rationales.quote: what about inventory?
rationales.explanation: Probes how inventory needs fit within the proposed financing plan.

rationales.quote: to get started with 2500 people, you got to buy inventory
rationales.explanation: Highlights substantial upfront inventory funding required for the projected customer base.

rationales.quote: But you said 2500 by end of the year.
rationales.explanation: Challenges the feasibility of reaching the stated customer target on the proposed timeline.

rationales.quote: That’s six months.
rationales.explanation: Emphasizes that the customer-growth target must be achieved within only six months.

rationales.quote: And that accounts for all the different size variations?
rationales.explanation: Tests whether the inventory approach can cover size variation.

rationales.quote: And different styles?
rationales.explanation: Tests whether the inventory approach can also cover style variation.

rationales.quote: I can really see people using it.
rationales.explanation: Expresses positive belief that consumers would use the product.

rationales.quote: I have concerns about the operations and logistical part of it.
rationales.explanation: States concern about the operational and logistics execution required.

rationales.quote: the inventory issue is… is capital intensive
rationales.explanation: Warns that inventory will require substantial capital.

rationales.quote: marketing hasn’t been tested really
rationales.explanation: Notes that the customer-acquisition approach lacks meaningful validation.

rationales.quote: if you can convince me of the operational piece I may come in as an angel investor. But I’m going to pass for now.
rationales.explanation: Explicitly ties the current refusal to unresolved operational concerns.

rationales.quote: And this is the opposite!
rationales.explanation: Contrasts the company's unusually low fundraising valuation with the investors' usual concern about excessive pricing.

rationales.quote: He should raise 500 grand now.
rationales.explanation: States that the proposed raise is insufficient for the business's needs.

rationales.quote: It’s going to cost more than he thinks, I believe.
rationales.explanation: Explains that underestimated costs make the current financing plan inadequate.

rationales.quote: I liked him a lot.
rationales.explanation: Expresses a positive personal assessment of the founder.

post-pitch interviews, later diligence and subsequent updates; teaser is an opening preview/repeated future clip. Use unclear

merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.

rationales.quote: $50 a week?
rationales.explanation: Clarifies the service's pricing cadence.

rationales.quote: So it’s not really a week.
rationales.explanation: Challenges whether the package actually provides the represented week of clothing.

rationales.quote: Well what’s involved with that? Why is that holding you back?
rationales.explanation: Probes the operational bottleneck preventing the company from serving more customers.

rationales.quote: It seems like that becomes a real stumbling point.
rationales.explanation: Identifies styling and inventory operations as a significant obstacle to scaling the solution.

rationales.quote: But there are a lot of different size combinations.
rationales.explanation: Raises concern that numerous garment and shoe combinations complicate efficient inventory reuse.

rationales.quote: And then what’s your acquisition cost?
rationales.explanation: Requests a key measure of customer-acquisition efficiency.

rationales.quote: this is a customer acquisition business, right? umm And I don’t know if you’re planning to bring someone in ...
rationales.explanation: Identifies marketing as central to success while questioning whether the company has a plan to add that capability.

rationales.quote: Ideally it should be someone on your team.
rationales.explanation: Argues that the essential marketing capability should be owned internally rather than outsourced.

rationales.quote: At a senior level.
rationales.explanation: States that the needed internal marketing hire must have senior-level expertise.

rationales.quote: what about inventory?
rationales.explanation: Probes how the proposed financing plan will cover inventory requirements.

rationales.quote: But to get started with 2500 people, you got to buy inventory.
rationales.explanation: Highlights the upfront inventory investment required to support the projected customer base.

rationales.quote: But you said 2500 by end of the year.
rationales.explanation: Challenges whether the financing and inventory plan can support the stated customer target.

rationales.quote: That’s six months.
rationales.explanation: Emphasizes the short timeline available to achieve the projected growth.

rationales.quote: And that accounts for all the different size variations?
rationales.explanation: Tests whether the proposed inventory approach can operationally cover customer size variation.

rationales.quote: And different styles?
rationales.explanation: Tests whether the inventory approach can also accommodate style variation.

rationales.quote: I think it’s a very smart idea. I see the value to consumers. I can really see people using it.
rationales.explanation: Expresses a positive personal assessment of the idea's consumer value and likely appeal.

rationales.quote: I have concerns about the operations and logistical part of it.

rationales.quote: the inventory issue is… is capital intensive You’re going to have to spend a lot of money for inventory.

rationales.quote: marketing hasn’t been tested really

rationales.quote: if you can convince me of the operational piece I may come in as an angel investor. But I’m going to pass for now.
rationales.explanation: Explicitly makes investment contingent on resolving the operational-feasibility concern and passes in the meantime.

rationales.quote: And this is the opposite!

rationales.quote: It’s going to cost more than he thinks, I believe.
